text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- In Budapest yesterday Czech Premier Vaclav Klaus declared that his country and Hungary share identical interests, and noted that the two leaderships conduct an intense political dialogue on integration issues.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs conferred with his German counterpart Klaus Kinkel in Bonn on Monday.

- Parliament will decide today whether to set up a parliamentary commission to investigate companies founded by political parties and the parties' real estate holdings, as proposed by the Young Democrats.

- The vice-president of the Agricultural Producers Interest Protection Organisation (Metesz) warned on Monday that unless a substantive agreement is reached with the government within 72 hours, Metesz will start closing down national borders and roads leading to the capital.

- Lakaskassza Rt and Fundamenta Rt are expected to receive foundation licenses from the State Money and Capital Markets Supervision in the next few days, enabling them to grant loans for the purchase, renovation, reconstruction, sale or construction of homes.
NEPSZABADSAG

- This paper cites anonymous sources that the members of the World Trade Organisation panel have not yet been named because Hungary and the four countries that have filed a complaint against the level of Hungary's agricultural subsidies are trying to reach an out-of-court settlement.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Budapest Mayor Gabor Demszky is paying an official visit to South Africa.
- A senior official with the Hungarian Truckers Society is appealing to the UN Economic Committee for Europe regarding Hungarian trucks detained by Russia since last year.
- The Budapest City Council will vote on the HUF 3.1 billion World Bank loan to upgrade sewage treatment at its March 27 meeting.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- As a result of the country's improving economic situation, the German bank Kreditanstalt fur Wiederaufbau will grant loans to Hungary on more favourable terms than two years ago, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy told the economic cabinet.
- Gaz de France and its representative Cashline Broker have purchased a 35 percent stake in the south Hungarian gas supplier Degaz from 180 towns.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- Foreign joint ventures operating in Hungary exported a total of $7.27 billion last year, 55.3 percent of the country's total exports, but also imported $9.9 billion, 61 percent of the total, to produce an aggregate foreign trade deficit of $2.6 billion.
- The tender for the selection of a privatisation consultant for Mezobank closed without success.
- The consortium comprising Ruhrgas AG and VEW Energie AG will raise its stake in the southwest Hungarian gas supplier Ddgaz from athe current 50 percent plus one vote to 90 percent.
- MOL's oil and gas facility near Szeged was awarded an ISO 9002 quality certificate on the weekend.
- Last week's domestic Mezogep share issue was two times oversubscribed, mainly by Hungarian pension funds and banks.
- The German broker Ballmeier and Schultz has been quoting prices for Agrimpex shares in the free market category of the Frankfurt Stock Exchange since Monday.
